correctness.rationale: The period-doubling fixed point satisfies p[2i]=0, p[2i+1]=1-p[i] and p[i]=v_2(i+1) mod 2. Each factor recurs at infinitely many 2-adically shifted positions. A complete gap-parity analysis determines the one-symbol base spectra. The exact two decimation identities reduce all mixed-window spectra to strictly shorter window lengths; the chosen dyadic shift is divisible by all lower periods. The two-symbol exact table and sharp least period follow by explicit substitution. The standalone script returned VERIFY_OK on 34031 bounded finite assertions; proof, not finite samples, establishes all quantifiers.

value.rationale: The complete all-length, all-separation paired-end factor classification is motivated by an established boundary-sequence invariant in combinatorics on words and paired-end reconstruction. It turns a known automatic sequence of boundary sets into a purely periodic sequence with an explicit uniform period, including unequal window lengths; the exact two-window table demonstrates a nontrivial three-state example and a sharp lower-order period. This is a structural infinite theorem, not a finite or arbitrary cutoff.
